Title: A Very Long Announcement That Will Need Trimming
Body: This row exists to prove the one-slide guarantee holds even when someone pastes far too much text into a single cell. The kiosk first shrinks the type to make it fit, and if it still will not fit at a size anyone could read from across the hall, it trims the text on a word boundary and points people to the bulletin instead of rendering a wall of unreadable grey. Nobody wants to squint at a television from thirty feet away, and an announcement nobody can read is worse than no announcement at all, because it takes up a slot that a legible announcement could have used. The alternative designs are all worse: continuing onto a second slide breaks the promise that one announcement equals one screen, scrolling text is difficult to read and looks cheap, and simply letting the text overflow means the last few lines vanish off the bottom edge where nobody will ever see them. So we shrink, then we trim, and we tell the editor about it in the import tool so the text can be shortened properly before Sunday. This paragraph is now comfortably longer than anything a real parish announcement would ever be, which is exactly the point of including it here.
